title: Prospective observational study on tibial plateau fractures
summary:
Fractures of the upper part of the shinbone involving the knee joint can lead to long-term pain, restricted mobility, and difficulties in everyday life, sports, and professional activities. Although various treatment options are available, little is currently known about how symptoms and quality of life develop over several years and which factors influence the recovery process.

The aim of our study is to investigate long-term treatment outcomes and patient satisfaction following such fractures. In particular, we aim to determine how well patients regain their previous mobility and physical function, when they are able to return to work and sporting activities, and whether additional treatments become necessary over time. Furthermore, we will examine whether treatment outcomes differ depending on the type of treatment, the severity of the injury, and the patient's health insurance status.

For this purpose, a total of 100 patients treated for such fractures at the University Medical Center Göttingen will be followed over a period of five years. Both surgically and non-surgically treated patients will be included. Follow-up assessments will be conducted at 6, 12, 24, 36, 48, and 60 months. During these assessments, participants will complete standardized questionnaires addressing their symptoms, mobility, satisfaction, and limitations in daily activities. In addition, a physical examination will be performed by a physician. Additional X-ray examinations will only be performed if medically indicated due to existing symptoms.

The findings of this study are expected to contribute to a better understanding of long-term recovery and to help improve treatment and follow-up care for future patients.
conditions: Fracture of upper end of tibia

interventions.name:
Following recruitment, participants will undergo follow-up assessments at 6, 12, 24, 36, 48, and 60 months after surgical treatment or initiation of conservative treatment, respectively.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with tibial plateau fractures treated at the Department of Trauma Surgery, Orthopaedics and Plastic Surgery at the University Medical Center Göttingen will be included, regardless of whether they undergo surgical or conservative treatment.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients unable to provide informed consent
Patients under 18 years of age
Pregnant patients
